title: Apple’s new iPhone camera mode promises to prove your photo isn’t AI
slides: Apple's new camera mode promises to prove your photo isn't AI—but how?
It captures a unique signature at the moment of shooting.
The signature can be faked if attackers gain access to the hardware.
You can now verify your photos with a simple tap.
Start using it today to protect your visual truth.
thread_text:
1. The AI photo arms race just escalated

Apple's new camera mode captures a unique signature at the moment of shooting, promising to prove your photo isn't AI-generated. Can it actually work?

2. How the signature works

It's a cryptographic fingerprint embedded in the image data right when you press the shutter. That makes it nearly impossible to fake after the fact.

3. But it's not foolproof

If attackers gain access to the hardware, they can replicate the signature. So the system only works if your device stays secure.

4. Verification is just a tap

Anyone can verify a photo's authenticity with a simple tap. No special tools or technical knowledge required.

5. Your move: test it today

Take a photo with the new mode and try to verify it. If you haven't, you're already behind on protecting your visual truth.

instagram.caption:
Your next photo can carry proof it wasn't generated by AI. 📸

Apple added a camera mode that stamps a unique signature the moment you press the shutter.

That mark is tied to the image data itself, so faking it afterward is hard.

But if someone gets inside the hardware, they can copy the signature.

If you publish photos, a single tap now lets anyone check they're real — and that puts the burden on you to use it.

Have you tried shooting with the new mode yet? 🔐
